newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 20.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company -- BARCLAYS CHIEF TO HEAD TAX AND BENEFIT TASKFORCE

Martin Taylor, chief executive of Barclays Bank, has been appointed to head a Whitehall taskforce of senior civil servants which aims to reform the tax and benefits system. The taskforce will attempt to modernize the system in hopes of improving work incentives and lowering dependence on welfare. The appointment of Taylor is an example of a Labour government pledge to work closely with the business community, also demonstrated through the appointment of former BP chairman Sir David Simon to a ministerial role and peerage.
-- EXCHANGE TIGHTENS OVER AIM FLOTATIONS

The UK Alternative Investment Market (Aim), set up to provide development capital to young and growing companies, will soon be subject to new government rules demanding the naming of any individual or organisation promoting a company seeking to be listed. The government initiative was taken as a means of eliminating the possibility of listing potentially vulnerable companies. While the stock exchange claims it had little knowledge of share prices being falsely augmented, it did agree that investors should know exactly who is bringing a company to Aim.
-- DEUTSCHE BANK TO REDUCE DOMESTIC SHAREHOLDINGS

Rolf Breuer, the new chairman of Deutsche Bank, is set to take initiatives to reduce the bank's holdings in some of Germany's largest businesses, focusing instead on foreign investments, with a goal of 50-50 holdings in each by the next century. The 10.7 billion stg move would decrease the influence German banks have over industry and provide higher shareholder value to investors. Previously, high tax rates in Germany had prevented the bank from reducing its stake in local companies.
-- EMI IN TALKS OVER PLAN TO SELL MUSIC ONLINE

UK record company EMI has announced plans to begin selling its products over the Internet, the first record company to take such an initiative. While it is currently possible to digitally transfer music over the World Wide Web, piracy and retail relationships had prevented any record companies from previously doing business over the Internet. EMI is in negotiations with french group Eurodat, who earlier this year began a pilot music sales project operating similar to a jukebox, and run by French cable TV company Lyonnaise des Eaux.
-- TOBACCO ADVERTISING BAN TO INCLUDE SPORT SPONSORSHIP

UK health secretary Frank Dobson confirmed that the government's draft tobacco advertising bill will include a ban on sports sponsorship, much to the surprise of the industry and sport. The government will give sport adequate time in which to find more "benign" sponsors as it realized many sports "are heavily dependent on tobacco sponsorship". It has been estimated that the tobacco industry spends eight million stg per year on sports sponsorship in the UK, and industry officials are said to be "very disappointed" following the government announcement.
-- NEC TO BOOST MEMORY CHIP OUTPUT ON HOPES OF UPTURN

Japanese semiconductor maker NEC is planning to increase memory production by 18 percent this year following an improved outlook for the market. The move from NEC follows a period when most chip-makers have scaled back production and expansion plans in the wake of a sharp downturn in memory prices last year.
-- GLAXO WARNS ON THE STRONG POUND

Pharmaceuticals and healthcare giant Glaxo Wellcome has warned that the strength of sterling will reduce earnings for 1997 by about 5 percent. The warning came as the group announced it had achieved faster-than-expected sales growth in the first four months of the year. Sales in the four months to April 30 were 2.75 billion stg, an increase of 10 percent on the same period last year.
-- SHIELD WINS LICENCE

Biotechnology company Shield Diagnostics has been awarded an exclusive licence to develop a test for thrombosis based on technology developed at the University of Glasgow. Under the terms of the licence, Shield will attempt to commercialise a new method for measuring homocysteine, a blood-based amino acid which has been identified with a higher risk of thrombosis.
-- JONES MAY SELL STAKE IN CWC

US cable company Jones Intercable is reported to be considering selling its stake in the newly formed UK telecoms and cable group Cable & Wireless Communications. Jones would be the first significant shareholder to leave the company, which was formed earlier this year by the merger of Mercury, Nynex CableComms, Videotron and Bell Cablemedia. Jones holds a 2.5 percent stake in CWC, which would be worth about 120 million stg on the open market.
-- GO-AHEAD GIVEN FOR ENDESA SALE

The Spanish government has approved plans for an October sale of the more than 50 percent stake it owns in Endesa, the country's dominant power group. The disposal, expected to be worth some $7 billion, will be Spain's biggest to date, and underlines the government's confidence in the domestic stock market.
